edges.limitations: The animals are wild-type mice transduced in adulthood with a human CA12(E143K) cDNA, so the experiment reports what the allele does to an otherwise normal gland rather than what lifelong biallelic loss of CA12 does to a developing one. No sweat chloride or sweat electrolyte measurement is reported, and the mouse does not carry a human-like distribution of eccrine sweat glands.

nodes.description: The eccrine duct normally reabsorbs sodium and chloride from the primary sweat, so sweat emerging at the skin surface is hypotonic. With reduced CA XII catalysis ductal AE2 activity is lost, so chloride (and the sodium that follows it) is not reclaimed and remains in the duct lumen. The route to that loss is not settled: in mouse salivary gland and expression models the misfolded CA12(E143K) protein is retained in the endoplasmic reticulum, whereas in polarized MDCK cells the same variant reached the basolateral membrane with activity lost instead through chloride inhibition. Both were studied outside the sweat duct, so the molecular route there is inferred.

nodes.description: CA XII is not confined to the sweat duct: it is the major bicarbonate supplier for the ductal anion exchanger AE2 in salivary and pancreatic gland ducts as well, so the same loss of function reduces salivary ductal fluid and bicarbonate secretion. Delivering the human CA12(E143K) allele to mouse salivary glands inhibits ductal fluid secretion and salivation, and patients homozygous for that allele report a dry mouth and dry tongue. This is a parallel consequence of the molecular lesion rather than a step in the sweat-duct chain.

nodes.description: Carbonic anhydrase XII catalyses the reversible hydration of carbon dioxide to bicarbonate and a proton. CA XII is localized basolaterally in the reabsorptive duct of the human eccrine sweat gland; its role as the major bicarbonate supplier for the ductal Cl--HCO3- exchanger AE2 was demonstrated directly in salivary and pancreatic ducts, and is inferred for the sweat duct. Reduced CA XII catalysis (through diminished activity, chloride inhibition shown directly for the E143K allele, or ER retention of the misfolded protein in expression models) lowers local bicarbonate available to drive anion exchange.
